findings.evidence: http://HOST/ (HTTP 200) serves only 133 characters (17 words) of extractable body text; the element #js-content is empty in the raw HTML and is populated at runtime by inline JavaScript carrying 1440 characters of markup (82 words) across 1 injection sites. Facts visible only after JS execution include the prices "$120, $149, $299, $499".

suggested_action.mechanism: Most AI retrieval pipelines index the raw HTTP response; content injected by the browser after load is invisible to them, so JS-only facts are simply absent from the model's evidence.
suggested_action.summary: Server-side render (SSR) or statically pre-render the product, pricing and company sections into the initial HTML response for #js-content inside <main>, keeping JavaScript for enhancement only, and mirror the same values in Product/Offer JSON-LD structured data. Verify with a text-only fetch (`curl`) that the raw HTML already carries the prices, so the facts are machine-readable for AI crawlers and assistants that never execute JavaScript and can be extracted and cited.

findings.title: Business-critical content is only present after client-side JavaScript execution

findings.evidence: http://HOST/ (HTTP 200) yields only 133 characters (17 words) of extractable text, and 4 of 4 fact families are absent from it (missing: company_facts, contact, pricing, product_detail). The page advertises 1 fact sections (Acme Cloud Solutions) but supplies no prices, contact details or company figures in HTML text. Root cause measured on this page: client-side rendering. A simulated render recovers 82 words that a text-only crawler never sees, starting "Our Products AcmeKube Fully managed Kubernetes platform with automated".

suggested_action.mechanism: Retrieval-augmented assistants chunk and embed the text of the HTTP response. If the response has no facts, the site is either omitted from the answer or represented by a competitor's page that does state them.
suggested_action.summary: Publish the product, pricing, company and contact facts as server-rendered HTML text in the initial response - real <h2> headings, paragraphs and tables rather than JavaScript payloads or images - and back them with Organization and Product JSON-LD structured data. Then verify with a text-only fetch: whatever `curl` returns is the machine-readable evidence an AI assistant can extract, quote and cite.
